title: One question left before we build

steps.headline: Should the Contribute screen tell you when your work is saved nowhere but this device?
steps.today: The Contribute screen explains what contributing is, opens the five steps, and offers one button: Set up development workspace. It says nothing at all about backup. Backup lives somewhere else — Settings → Cross-Device Backup & Sync — where it already turns red and says Sync Failing when it breaks.
steps.problem: You already decided setup should let you start on this device even when backup cannot connect. That is the right call, but it means you can work for days on a project that exists on this laptop only, and this screen would never say so. Last round I showed a made-up backup failure here and you answered "confused?" — fairly, since it was an invented failure sitting where your real status would go. No invented state will be shown again; this asks the real question instead.
steps.proposal: Three ways this screen can handle backup. Pick the one you would want on the day it actually matters.

options.label: Speak up only when it's broken
pros: Nothing extra to read on a normal day — the screen stays as short as you approved it.
The one line only appears when the news is worth your attention.
It reports your real backup, never an example.
cons: You never get a positive "this is backed up" confirmation; silence means fine.
A state you rarely see is a state that is rarely tested — it needs its own test to stay honest.

options.label: Always show where it's saved
options.summary: A permanent line under the explanation, saying either that this project is backed up or that it lives on this device only.
pros: You can always tell without going to another screen.
One consistent place to look, whatever the answer is.
cons: A line that says the same thing almost every day stops being read — so it may be invisible on the one day it changes.
Adds a row to a screen you already told me was cluttered.

options.label: Leave backup out of it
options.summary: The Contribute screen never mentions backup. Backup problems stay in the backup settings, which already show a red dot and Sync Failing.
pros: The simplest screen, and the one you approved unchanged.
One screen owns backup, so there is no second copy of the truth to fall out of date.
cons: You could start a contribution project that is saved nowhere and never be told at the moment it starts.
You would only find out by happening to open a different settings page.
